description:
Reverse propagation: jmap-metadata-server's MemoryBackend.create_object has a defense-in-depth account guard at memory.rs:680-692 that refuses to silently auto-register an unknown account when a caller bypasses the handler-layer accountNotFound check (e.g. test seeders, future direct trait callers). Canonical mail-server's MemoryBackend at memory.rs:955+ does NOT have this guard.

This is the rare case where the sibling got the pattern right and the canonical needs to follow. Per workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template propagation rule, the right move is to:
1. Add the same defense-in-depth guard to jmap-mail-server's MemoryBackend.create_object (canonical).
2. Audit and add it to 6 other extension-server siblings (chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing) that share the canonical's lax shape.

Rationale (per metadata-server's own rustdoc at memory.rs:680-686): 'a backend create_object is also called directly from test seeders and from any future caller that bypasses the handler. Silently extending known_accounts on a per-object call would mean a stray create attaches private metadata records to a phantom account.' The same reasoning applies to every extension's data type (Email/Mailbox/Calendar/Task/Contact/FileNode/SharingPrincipal).

Engineering impact: prevents a class of state-corruption bugs where a fixture or future API caller bypasses accountNotFound enforcement. Worst-case under the current (un-guarded) canonical pattern: an undeclared account silently materialises with one stray record, no error surfaces, and later /get/changes/query against that account succeed against partial data.

Discovered while triaging bd:JMAP-826m.42 (positive-observation bead noting that metadata-server's guard exists).
title: Workspace-canonical-first reverse propagation: defense-in-depth account guard in MemoryBackend.create_object — propagate metadata-server pattern up to canonical mail-server, then to 7 siblings
